newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S. envoy urges Bosnian Serbs to abide by laws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy urges Bosnian Serbs to abide by laws.

text.p: United States envoy Robert Gelbard called on feuding Bosnian Serb leaders on Tuesday to respect the rule of law and abide by a constitution set out under a peace agreement.
Gelbard spoke cautiously about political turmoil in Bosnia's Serb republic a day after Serb President Biljana Plavsic accused hardliners of preparing a coup against her.
"Obviously I'm aware there are disagreements among the authorities of Republika Srpska (Serb republic)," Gelbard told reporters in Sarajevo.
"What we expect is that under any circumstances the constitutional framework of Republika Srpska and Bosnia-Herzegovina will be strictly obeyed."
Asked how the international community would respond if Bosnian Serb authorities violated their own constitution, Gelbard said: "Never answer hypothetical questions."

Plavsic was detained on Sunday night by Yugoslav and Bosnian Serb police upon her return from a trip to Britain. After her release, she accused ex-president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic of trying to oust her from office.
Karadzic still wields power in Serb-controlled territory in coordination with Momcilo Krajisnik, the Serb member of the Bosnian collective presidency.
Gelbard declined to discuss Plavsic's accusations and said he had held talks with Plavsic on Friday and with Krajisnik over the weekend.

"We continue to support President Plavsic in her duly elected role as the constitutional president of Republika Srpska but we also support those other officials in their roles including President Krajisnik."

Gelbard said none of the Serb leaders were fulfilling their obligations under the 1995 Dayton peace agreement ending the war in Bosnia. He expressed outrage at their failure to restructure the Serb police force under terms set out by United Nations police monitors.
Gelbard referred to an incident in which a Serb police officer had refused to hand over his pistol to U.S. peacekeeping troops at an illegal checkpoint last week.
He said the international community and the NATO-led peace Stabilisation Force (SFOR) would not tolerate unauthorised checkpoints limiting free movement across old front lines.
"We are astonished at the stupidity of some police officers in Republika Srpska who are seeking confrontation with SFOR."
